items.text: More properties that descend
$g\colon S'\to S$ faithfully flat quasi-compact: $f$ affine, quasi-affine, integral, finite, quasi-finite $\iff$ $f'$ is.
Affine: $X'$ affine over $Y'$ with descent data is effective (affine descent): $X_1$ affine over $Y$ with $X_1'\simeq X'$; by 1-descent $X_1\simeq X$.

Quasi-affine: $f$ coherent and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}f_*\mathcal O_X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A$ an open immersion; $\mathcal A'=g^*\mathcal A$ (flat base change), so this open immersion is the descent of that for $f'$.
Integral/finite: $A\to A'$ faithfully flat, $B$ an $A$-algebra, $B'$ integral (finite) over $A'$ $\Rightarrow$ $B$ integral (finite) over $A$:
B=\varinjlim B_i\ (B_i\ \text{of finite type});\ \ B\ \text{integral}\iff B_i\ \text{finite over }A;\quad B_i'\subset B'\ \text{finite over }A'\Rightarrow B_i\ \text{finite}
Quasi-finite: finite type (descends) and finite fibres (only surjectivity of $S'\to S$ is used).
Ampleness descends
$\mathcal L$ invertible on $X$, $\mathcal L'$ its inverse image: $\mathcal L$ is ample (resp. very ample) relative to $f$ iff $\mathcal L'$ is relative to $f'$.
Very ample: (a) $f^*f_*\mathcal L\to\mathcal L$ surjective; (b) the induced morphism is an immersion.
\mathcal E=f_*\mathcal L:\qquad f^*\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L\ \ \leadsto\ \ X\longrightarrow\mathbf P(\mathcal E)\ \text{an immersion}

$f$ coherent (descends), so $\mathcal E'=g^*\mathcal E$; (a) holds after the faithfully flat $X'\to X$, hence before; $X\to\mathbf P(\mathcal E)$ is quasi-compact and an immersion after base change, hence an immersion.
\text{Ample: }\forall\ \mathcal F\ \text{quasi-coherent of finite type }\exists n:\ f^*f_*\mathcal F(n)\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F(n)\quad(Y\ \text{quasi-compact});\quad\text{descends as above}
Effectivity of descent data
$S'\to S$ faithfully flat quasi-compact, $X'$ over $S'$ with a gluing datum: $X''=p_1^*X'=p_2^*X'$ with $q_1,q_2\colon X''\rightrightarrows X'$ over $p_1,p_2$, both squares cartesian.
\begin{CD} X'' @>{q_1}>> X'\\ @V{q_2}VV @VVV\\ X' @>>> S \end{CD}
Descent data (cocycle condition) $\iff$ $X''\rightrightarrows X'$ is an equivalence relation on $X'$ (on-points: $X''(Z)\subset X'(Z)\times X'(Z)$).

General nonsense: $g$ of 1-descent for a fibred category with fibre products. Descent datum on $X'$ is effective $\iff$ the equivalence relation $X''$ is effective universal: the quotient $X$ exists, $X''=X'\times_XX'$, and this persists after any base change $X_1\to X$.
$g$ is of 1-descent iff it is an effective universal epimorphism ($S$ is the quotient of $S'$ by $S''$, universally).
Local criterion for effectivity
An open $X'_i\subset X'$ is stable if its two inverse images in $X''$ coincide (a set-theoretic condition); the induced descent data on $X'_i$ is defined.
$X'=\bigcup X'_i$ stable opens: descent datum on $X'$ is effective $\iff$ each induced datum on $X'_i$ is effective.
($\Rightarrow$) the stable $X'_i$ comes from $X_i\subset X$, and $X_i$ is the quotient of $X'_i$ by $X''_i=X'_i\times_{X_i}X'_i$.
($\Leftarrow$) glue the $X_i$ along the $X_{ij}$ (descents of the stable $X'_i\cap X'_j$).
The functor Phi
$R\rightrightarrows X'$ an equivalence relation with $p_1,p_2$ faithfully flat quasi-compact. For a variable $X_1$ put $\Phi(X_1)$ = isomorphism classes of
Z_1\to X_1\ \text{(1-descent)},\quad Z_1\to X',\quad Z_1\times_{X_1}Z_1\to R,\qquad\text{squares over }p_1,q_1\ \text{and}\ p_2,q_2\ \text{cartesian}
Rigid category (no non-trivial automorphisms); $\Phi$ is contravariant in $X_1$ and a sheaf for the Zariski topology.
If an effective universal quotient $X$ exists, then $\tilde X\to\Phi$ is an isomorphism; conversely, if $\Phi$ is representable, the representing object is the effective universal quotient.
Hence effectivity $\iff$ representability of $\Phi$; if $X'=\bigcup X'_i$ stable opens, $\Phi$ is covered by open subfunctors $\Phi_i$, representable iff each $\Phi_i$ is.
